units.source_text: 古歌：“绣床铺只袖，独寝正无聊。

en.t: An old poem says: On the embroidered bed I spread only one sleeve; sleeping alone is truly lonely.

units.source_text: 宇治桥神女，今宵盼待劳。”

en.t: The goddess of Uji Bridge waits longingly tonight, weary from expectation.
This appears in the Kokin Wakashu.

units.source_text: 古人独寝时，把睡衣的一只衣袖铺在席上，睡在这上面，表示怀人。

en.t: In ancient times, when people slept alone, they would spread one sleeve of their nightclothes on the mat and sleep on it to show that they were thinking of someone they loved.
